To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sunitinib, which is used in the treatment of renal cell carcinoma, is a potent inhibitor of caspase-11 and caspase-5.
the immunosuppressive drug sunitinib inhibits the production of IL-1β, a key pro-inflammatory cytokine that mediates the innate immune response to fungal pathogens.
sunitinib treatment induces the production of pro-inflammatory IL-1β, which in turn is responsible for the development of aspergillosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which the immune system recognises fungal PAMPs and how this recognition triggers the innate immune system to eliminate fungal pathogens.
the role of fungal PAMPs and fungal PRRs in fungal recognition by the immune system and the consequences for fungal pathogenicity.
the role of the fungal pathogen Aspergillus fumigatus as a PAMP and the role of the innate immune response in host defence against this pathogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aspergillus triggers the innate immune system by binding to fungal PAMPs and that this binding is sensed by PRRs.
the recognition and clearance of fungal PAMPs is a complex process involving multiple PRRs which in turn are coupled to a number of intracellular signalling complexes (inflammasomes).
the innate immune system is able to recognize Aspergillus as a foreign pathogen, and that the innate immune response is able to eliminate Aspergillus infection in the immunocompetence host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show a case of Aspergillosus fumigatus infection in a renal cell carcinoma patient with lung metastasis, who was treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) Sunitinib.
we have identified the fungal PRRs that are involved in the recognition of Aspergillus fumigatus and the generation of the host immune response.
the innate host defence system is able to recognise Aspergillus PAMPs via PRRs which are expressed on phagocytic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLRP3 inflammasome plays a key role in fungal clearance and that its activation in response to Aspergillus infection is dependent on fungal recognition by CLR.
the host immune system can be activated to combat the fungal pathogen by targeting the fungal pathogen’s ability to activate the host’s innate immune system.
the innate immune system of the immunocompromised host is not able to mount a sufficient response to clear fungal infection, leading to invasive aspergillosis.
